exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Derivative of a Parametric Curve

question.text: For the parametric curve \[x=t\sin{t}, \quad y=3\cos{t}, \qquad -\infty< t< \infty,\] find the derivative $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at the point $P$ on the curve where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}.$
question.explanation:
We will use the formula \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}. \]

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

\[x'(t) =t\cos{t} + \sin{t}, \qquad y'(t)=-3\sin{t}. \]

Therefore, \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{-3\sin{t}}{t\cos{t} + \sin{t}}=-\dfrac{3}{t\cot{t}+1}. \] At the point where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ we have \[ \begin{align} \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} &= -\,\frac{3}{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\cot{\dfrac{\pi}{2}} + 1}\\[3pt] &= -\,\frac{3}{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\cdot 0 + 1} \\[3pt] &= -\,3\,. \end{align} \]

example.title: Finding the Derivative of a Parametric Curve

question.text: For the parametric curve \[x=e^{2t}, \quad y=(t^2-1)e^{-t}, \qquad -\infty< t< \infty,\] find the derivative $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at the point $P$ on the curve where $t=1.$
question.explanation:
We will use the formula \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}. \]

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

\[x'(t) = 2\mathrm{e}^{2t}, \qquad y'(t)=(1+2t-t^2)e^{-t}. \]

Therefore, \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{(1+2t-t^2)e^{-t}}{2\mathrm{e}^{2t}}=\frac{1}{2}(1+2t-t^2)e^{-3t}. \]

At the point where $t=1$ we have \[ \begin{align} \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} &= \frac{1}{2}(1+2(1)-(1)^2)e^{-3(1)}\\[3pt] &= \frac{1}{2}(1+2-1)e^{-3} \\[4pt] &= e^{-3}\,. \end{align} \]

example.title: Finding the Derivative of a Parametric Curve

question.text: For the parametric curve (shown above) \[x=t^3-t, \quad y=t^2 - 4, \qquad -\infty< t< \infty,\] find the derivative $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at the point $P$ on the curve where $t=3.$
question.explanation:
We will use the formula \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}. \]

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

\[x'(t) =3t^2-1, \qquad y'(t)=2t. \]

Therefore, \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{2t}{3t^2-1}. \] At the point where $t=3$ we have \[ \begin{align} \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} &= \dfrac{2\cdot 3}{3(3^2)-1}\\[3pt] &= \dfrac{6}{27-1}\\[3pt] %&= \dfrac{6}{26}\\ &= \dfrac{3}{13}. \end{align} \]

example.title: Finding the Derivative of a Parametric Curve

question.text: For the parametric curve \[x=(t^3-1)e^t, \quad y=2\sin t, \qquad -\infty< t< \infty,\] find the derivative $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at the point $P$ on the curve where $t=0.$
question.explanation:
We will use the formula \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}. \]

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

\[x'(t) = (t^3+3t^2-1)e^t, \qquad y'(t)=2\cos{t}. \]

Therefore, \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{2\cos{t}}{(t^3+3t^2-1)e^t}. \]

At the point where $t=0$ we have \[ \begin{align} \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} &= \frac{2\cos{0}}{(0^3+3\cdot 0^2-1)e^0}\\[3pt] &= \frac{2(1)}{(-1)\cdot 1} \\[3pt] &= -2\,. \end{align} \]

example.title: Finding the Derivative of a Parametric Curve

question.text: For the parametric curve (shown above) \[x=3\sin{2t}, \quad y=4\cos{2t}, \qquad 0\leq t< 2\pi,\] find the derivative $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at the point $P$ on the curve where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{8}.$
question.explanation:
We will use the formula \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}. \]

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

\[x'(t) =6 \cos{2t}, \qquad y'(t)= -8\sin{2t}. \]

Therefore, \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{ -8\sin{2t}}{6 \cos{2t}}=-\dfrac{4}{3}\tan{2t}. \] At the point where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{8}$ we have \[ \begin{align} \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} &=- \,\dfrac{4}{3}\cdot \tan{\left(2\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{8}\right)} \\[3pt] &= - \,\dfrac{4}{3}\cdot \tan{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)} \\[3pt] &= - \,\dfrac{4}{3}\cdot 1 \\[3pt] &= -\,\dfrac{4}{3}\,. \end{align} \]

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent to a Parametric Curve at a Given Point

question.text: For the parametric curve \[ x=\sqrt{\sin\left(e^t\right)}, \quad y=\cot\left(e^t\right), \qquad -\infty < t < 1, \] calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\ln\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right).$
question.explanation:
We will use the formula \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}. \]

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

\begin{align} x'(t) &= \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{\sin\left(e^t\right)}}\cdot \cos\left(e^t\right)\cdot e^t\\[3pt] &= \dfrac{e^t \cos\left(e^t\right)}{2\sqrt{\sin\left(e^t\right)}}, \\[3pt] y'(t) &= -e^t\csc^2\left(e^t\right). \end{align}

So we have \begin{align} \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} &= \dfrac{-e^t\csc^2\left(e^t\right)}{\left(\dfrac{e^t \cos\left(e^t\right)}{2\sqrt{\sin\left(e^t\right)}}\right)} \\[3pt] &=-\,\dfrac{2\sqrt{\sin\left(e^t\right)}} {\sin^2\left(e^t\right)\cos\left(e^t\right)}\\[3pt] &=-\,\dfrac{2} {\sin^{3/2}\left(e^t\right)\cos\left(e^t\right)}\,. \end{align}

Therefore, when $t=\ln\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right),$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is \[ \begin{align} \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} &= -\,\dfrac{2} {\sin^{3/2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)}\\[3pt] &= -\,\dfrac{2} {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3/2}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)}\\[3pt] &= -2\cdot 2^{3/2}\,\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \\[3pt] &= -8\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}} \,. \end{align} \]

example.title: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent to a Parametric Curve at a Given Point

question.text: For the parametric curve \[ x=\sec^2{t}, \quad y=\csc^3{t}, \qquad 0< t < \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \] calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}.$
question.explanation:
We will use the formula \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}. \]

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

\[x'(t) = 2\sec^2{t}\tan{t}, \qquad y'(t)=- 3\csc^3{t}\cot{t}. \]

So we have \begin{align} \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} &= \dfrac{- 3\csc^3{t}\cot{t}}{2\sec^2{t}\tan{t}} \\[3pt] &= - 3\csc^3{t}\cot{t}\left( \frac{\cos^2{t}\cot{t}}{2}\right)\\[3pt] &=- \frac{3}{2}\,\csc^3{t}\cot^2{t}\cos^2{t} \\[3pt] &=- \frac{3}{2}\left( \frac{1}{\sin^3{t}}\right)\left( \frac{\cos^2{t}}{\sin^2{t}}\right)\cos^2{t}\\[3pt] &=- \frac{3}{2}\left( \frac{\cos^4{t}}{\sin^5{t}}\right)\\[3pt] &=- \frac{3}{2}\,\csc{t}\cot^4{t}\,. \end{align}

Therefore, when $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4},$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is \[ \begin{align} \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} &= - \frac{3}{2}\,\csc\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\cot^4\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\\[3pt] &= - \frac{3}{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}\cdot 1\\[3pt] &= - \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\, \\[3pt] &= -\dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\, . \end{align} \]

example.title: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent to a Parametric Curve at a Given Point

question.text: For the parametric curve \[ x=\sin(2t), \quad y=\cos^2(t), \qquad 0\leq t< 2\pi, \] calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{6}.$
question.explanation:
We will use the formula \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}. \]

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get \[x'(t) = 2 \cos(2t), \qquad y'(t)=-2\sin t\cos t=-\sin(2t). \]

So we have \begin{align} \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} &= \dfrac{-\sin(2t)}{2 \cos(2t)} \\[3pt] &= - \dfrac 12 \tan(2t). \end{align}

Therefore, when $t=\dfrac\pi 6,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is \begin{align} \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} &= -\,\frac{1}{2}\,\tan\left(\frac{2\pi}{6}\right)\\[3pt] &= -\,\frac{1}{2}\,\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\\[3pt] &= -\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \,. \end{align}

example.title: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent to a Parametric Curve at a Given Point

question.text: For the parametric curve \[ x=e^{t}-e^{-t}, \quad y=te^{t}, \qquad -\infty < t < \infty, \] calculate the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=0.$
question.explanation:
We will use the formula \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}. \]

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

\[x'(t) = e^{t}+e^{-t}, \qquad y'(t)=(t+1)e^{t}. \]

So we have \begin{align} \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} &= \dfrac{(t+1)e^{t}}{e^{t}+e^{-t}} \\[3pt] &=\dfrac{1+t}{1+e^{-2t}}. \end{align}

Therefore, when $t=0,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve is \[ \begin{align} \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} &= \frac{1+0}{1+e^{-0}}\\[3pt] &= \frac{1}{2} \,. \end{align} \]

example.title: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent to a Parametric Curve at a Given Point

question.text:
For the parametric curve 
\[
x = \ln(3t+1), \qquad y=te^{t}, \qquad -\dfrac{1}{3} <   t <   \infty,
\]
shown above, calculate the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=0.$ Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
We will use the formula \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}. \]

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get \[ x'(t) = \dfrac{3}{3t+1}, \qquad y'(t)=(t+1)e^{t}. \]

So, we have \begin{align} \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} &= \dfrac{(t+1)e^{t}}{\left( \dfrac{3}{3t+1} \right)} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{(t+1)(3t+1)e^{t}}{3}. \end{align}

Therefore, when $t=0,$ the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve is \begin{align} m=\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \, \Bigg|_{t\,=\,0} &= \dfrac{(0+1)(0+1)e^{0}}{3}\\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{1}{3}}. \end{align}
